harvestMonths.region: Stellenbosch, Western Cape (tunnel trial, planted June 2021)

evidence.quote: only the matured fruits were harvested (Lovelli et al., 2017; Patidar et al., 2018) from late October 2021 to January 2022.
evidence.doc: Tuaandi D (2023) The response of two Cape gooseberry varieties to organic amendments on degraded soils in the Western Cape, South Africa. MSc thesis, Stellenbosch University

harvestMonths.notes: Trial dates, not a grower recommendation: one season, in a tunnel at Welgevallen Experimental Farm, transplanted June 2021. 'late October' is month 10 and 'January' month 1; November and December are the span between them. Open-field timing and other planting months may differ. Page is the PDF page.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: The same thesis says 'The harvesting of the Cape gooseberry fruits started 120 days after transplanting.' (PDF p.28). That is days from transplanting in a tunnel, not years from planting a perennial, so no years value is stored.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Per-hectare only (e.g. 'the average yield of the Buffelsvlei gooseberry cultivar was 1191 kg ha-1', PDF p.35) with no per-plant figure; not converted.

pollination.notes: Not found in a fetched SA source.

gaps: Only one SA primary source: a single-season Stellenbosch tunnel trial. No open-field SA grower calendar from a government, ARC or grower body was found.
A seed company's sowing calendar (round 1) was excluded: nursery and seed-company pages are not used for harvest data.
Blocked: DALRRD/DAFF Cape gooseberry brochure (502), a 1986 tandfonline gooseberry paper (403), web.archive.org.
